paper.title_en: A gaseous anisotropic conformal star with near-linear Chaplygin effects in Tolman spacetime
paper.abstract_en: A gaseous charged anisotropic compact star model is developed by combining conformal symmetry with near-linear Chaplygin effects. The Chaplygin equation of state is useful in describing behaviour of exotic dark energy that believed to be the source of late accelerated universe expansion. Tolman ansatz is employed with a specific form of electric field to solve the Einstein–Maxwell field equations. Detailed analysis of the physical relativistic conditions is then conducted for model validation. The matter variables satisfy the regularity and energy conditions. The model’s stability through adiabatic indexes, equations of state parameters, speed of sound and ratio of mass to central density is satisfied. The balancing of the natural physical forces for equilibrium is obeyed as well. The mass–radius ratio and surface redshift are within acceptable ranges. The generated class of solution regained masses and radii of some well-known observed stars including 4U 1538-52, SMC X-1, and Her X-1. The strategy of employing conformal Killing vector with near-linear Chaplygin effects provides new insights in stellar modelling of relativistic stars. •We have generated a charged conformal star model with near-linear Chaplygin effects.•The Chaplygin EoS is useful in describing behaviour of exotic dark energy.•Tolman ansatz is used with a form of electric field to solve the field equations.•Physical analysis is conducted for model validation and comparison.•Masses of well-known stars 4U 1538-52, SMC X-1, and Her X-1 are regained.
